questions.question: Which Premier League club’s stadium roof famously became a viral swimming pool during a torrential downpour in May 2024, earning it the affectionate terrace nickname 'Waterfall Trafford'?
questions.explanation: Old Trafford suffered severe roof leaks during a 1–0 defeat to Arsenal, leading away fans to chant about taking a swim in the Stretford End.
questions.anchorClues: Old Trafford waterfall roof leak / Manchester United

questions.question: True or False: Manchester City officially lodged a comprehensive legal appeal in October 2026 following the independent commission's initial verdict regarding Premier League financial rule charges.
questions.explanation: Manchester City confirmed on 1 October 2026 that they had formally lodged an appeal against the commission's opinion, maintaining their innocence.
questions.anchorClues: Manchester City legal appeal / Premier League financial charges October 2026

questions.question: Which young manager hit the ground running with an unbeaten month in August 2024, becoming the youngest permanent manager to win a Premier League Manager of the Month award?
questions.explanation: Brighton boss Fabian Hürzeler took the award in August 2024 aged just 31 years and 173 days, following wins over Everton and Manchester United.
questions.anchorClues: Fabian Hürzeler youngest Manager of the Month / Brighton

questions.question: Which club held the record for conceding the fewest goals in a single Premier League home campaign, shipping just 4 goals on home turf in 2001–02?
questions.explanation: Fulham allowed just 4 opposition goals at Craven Cottage during the 2001–02 top-flight season, setting an incredibly tight defensive record.
questions.anchorClues: Fulham 4 goals conceded at home / Craven Cottage 2001–02

questions.question: True or False: Middlesbrough became the first team in Premier League history to field a starting XI composed entirely of 11 English players for a match in May 2006.
questions.explanation: Steve McClaren named an all-English starting 11 against Fulham on the final day of the 2005–06 season, resting key stars ahead of the UEFA Cup final.

questions.question: Which player scored the fastest ever Premier League hat-trick after coming off the bench, striking three times in just 19 minutes against Nottingham Forest in February 1999?
questions.explanation: Ole Gunnar Solskjær came on in the 72nd minute at the City Ground and bagged four goals, complete with an 8-minute blitz between his 1st and 3rd goals.
questions.anchorClues: Ole Gunnar Solskjær substitute hat-trick / Manchester United vs Nottingham Forest

questions.question: Which squad number was assigned to James Milner upon his transfer to Aston Villa from Newcastle United in the summer of 2008?
questions.explanation: James Milner took over the vacant number 7 shirt at Villa Park following his permanent £12m arrival from St. James' Park.
questions.anchorClues: James Milner squad number 7 / Aston Villa 2008

questions.question: Which referee holds the all-time record for issuing the most red cards in Premier League history, sending off 89 players across his top-flight officiating career?
questions.explanation: Mike Dean handed out a record 89 red cards during his 560 Premier League matches between 2000 and 2022.
questions.anchorClues: Mike Dean 89 red cards record / Premier League referee

questions.question: Which club scored 102 Premier League goals in the 2009–10 campaign, becoming the first side in top-flight history to breach the 100-goal mark in a single season?
questions.explanation: Carlo Ancelotti's Chelsea set a then-record 103 goals (later adjusted to 102 officially in statistical record books due to an own-goal ruling) on their way to the double.

questions.question: Which Nigerian forward holds the record for scoring in the most consecutive Premier League appearances for Everton, finding the net in 7 straight matches during the 1994–95 season?
questions.explanation: Daniel 'The Bull' Amokachi went on a blistering scoring run in the winter of 1994–95 for Joe Royle's Everton side.
questions.anchorClues: Daniel Amokachi consecutive goalscoring record / Everton 1994–95
